title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the combinatorial set-up for the boundary structure of M_{g,ν}.

Setting from the previous page. A 'standard' curve X is a curve with ordinary double points, marked by its points at infinity I. Its normalization of the completion is Y = X̂~, with components Y_α indexed by the vertices α ∈ S of the dual graph G_X. A is the set of edges, coming from the double points. Ã is the set of oriented edges (half-edges), a double cover of A, with a map to S.

Definitions on this page.
- (16) The marked weight of a vertex is ν_α = card I_α, where I_α is the fibre of I → S over α. It counts the points at infinity lying on the component.
- (17) The total weight is ν̂_α = ν_α + w_α. Here w_α, the 'order' of α, is card Ã_α, the number of half-edges leaving α. In modern terms it is the valence, with a loop counted twice.
- Hence ν̂_α is the number of special points on Y_α: the preimages of the nodes plus the marked points.

Section 3, 'Stable curves and MD-graphs'. A standard curve over an algebraically closed field is called stable if it satisfies one of the following equivalent conditions:
- (a) Aut X is finite;
- (b) for every α, the pointed curve (Y_α, I_α ∪ Ã_α) is 'anabelian', i.e. 2g_α + ν̂_α ≥ 3, i.e. 2g_α − 2 + ν̂_α ≥ 1.

The next page lists the remaining conditions: g=1 ⇒ ν̂ ≥ 1 and g=0 ⇒ ν̂ ≥ 3; no nonzero vector fields vanishing on the special points; the automorphism scheme is finite étale. It then defines MD-curves as stable and connected, and MD-graphs (stable graphs) as their combinatorial types.

This is the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen stability criterion, phrased on the dual graph decorated with genera and legs. It serves to describe the strata at infinity of the compactified M_{g,ν} combinatorially.
errors: No mathematical errors. The equivalences in (b) are correct: 2g+ν̂ ≥ 3 ⟺ 2g−2+ν̂ ≥ 1 ⟺ (g=0 ⇒ ν̂ ≥ 3; g=1 ⇒ ν̂ ≥ 1; g ≥ 2 automatic).

Small implicit point: 'Aut X' must mean automorphisms respecting the marking (X is the open curve, so this is automatic). The valence w_α correctly counts a loop twice only because Ã is the set of half-edges, as stated ('nb d'arcs sortant de α').

ideas.what: Marked weight and total weight (valence plus legs) of a vertex of a decorated dual graph
ideas.modern_name: Valence/number of special points n(v) of a vertex in a stable graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in Deligne–Mumford (1969) and Knudsen (1983) framework; graph formalism in Kontsevich, Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998)

ideas.what: Stability of a nodal curve: Aut finite ⟺ each normalized component with its special points is hyperbolic (2g−2+n > 0)
Use of the word 'anabélienne' for a pointed curve with 2g−2+n > 0
ideas.modern_name: Hyperbolic curve (anabelian curve in Grothendieck's terminology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme 1984, letter to Faltings 1983)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; letter to Faltings (1983)

ideas.what: 'MD-graphes' as the combinatorial types of stable connected curves (on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Stable graphs / dual graphs of stable curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; formalized by Kontsevich (1992) and Getzler–Kapranov (1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower, but not this graph formalism explicitly

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but standard definitions: dual graph weights and DM stability. The only Grothendieck-specific touches are the terminology ('anabélienne', 'MD-graphes', 'maquette'). Nothing here is new relative to the later literature on stable graphs.
transcription_corrections: The marginal note reads 'c'est le nb des pts à l'infini de la composante' and glosses ν_α. The main line reads 'ν_α = card I_α (où I_α est la fibre de I en α ∈ S)'.
The heading reads '3. Courbes "stables" et MD-graphes.' The insertion '(sur k alg. clos)' belongs after 'Une courbe standard'.
